meaning: Titles and reading notes drafted by an AI agent in the register of the paper they annotate. No mathematician has reviewed them.

notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.modeRadia: This closes the CellFormula proposition from RelRadialCoef; the same local name in ModeRadialPartsA closes the different CellAnalysis proposition from ResolvedEnergySt.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.ClassCoverS: There is no exact named provider or consumer in the supplied slice; GivenModelCover.classCover_of is a specialized analogue with mesh, model and harmonic-cover assumptions, not a proof of this generic interface.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.ClassInvers: No theorem with this exact interface as its named result and no theorem referring to its name were found in the supplied library. Its universal requirement with constant 2/3 is distinct from inverseSquareConst_two, which supplies InverseSquareConstStatement with constant 2.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.ExtendSegme: The supplied source slice has no exact named provider or consumer of this proposition; this is a declared interface, not a proved result in this file.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.RotationLea: This uses the totalized integral and ENNReal.toReal conventions, so the identity alone does not assert a finite L2 norm.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.RowModeGrad: The totalized integral and ENNReal.toReal conventions do not by themselves assert that the field has finite L2 norm.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.SixthPowerC: No theorem with this exact interface as its named result and no theorem referring to its name were found in the supplied library. This records the status of the named interface; it does not assert that the mathematical estimate is false.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.harmonicWei: The horizontal and vertical Fourier energies are divided by (|k|+1/2)² and (|k|+3/2)² respectively, and multiplied by the spatial radius squared. These shifted denominators are part of the definition.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.inverseSqua: The parameter is the norm constant H=2 in InverseSquareConstStatement; the squared-energy inequality therefore contains H²=4.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Spectral.shapeGradCoe: The angular coefficient uses max(r, innerRadius) in its denominator. On a positive-radius cell this agrees with the intended inverse-radius coefficient, while the definition stays total outside that cell.
notes.Breakdown.FracInternal.FrameInverseSquar: The proposition assumes the stated vanishing at the centre. Its name does not by itself assert oddness of the function on the whole interval.
